Subject: Mutual action plan: evaluation tests, exit owners & go/no-go timeline

Claire —

Thanks for the time yesterday. Attached is a first-pass MAP for the evaluation phase (MAP_ACME_v1.xlsx) plus a short pack of acceptance vignettes. The key asks in this email are: 1) confirm the owner for each exit gate, 2) validate the acceptance tests we put next to each success criterion, and 3) confirm a go/no-go decision date so we can reserve Dedicated capacity for the pilot cutover.

High-level (proposal):
- Evaluation window: 6 weeks (start: 2025-07-07)
- Go/no-go review: 2025-08-18 (lead: Claire + Acme product + Redwood CS)
- Success criteria we think matter: functional pass rate, P95 latency, hallucination/tolerance bounds, data routing & retention checks, and security evidence (SOC2 audit items).

I've put concrete acceptance tests in the spreadsheet. A few specific Qs for you ahead of the alignment call next week: 
1) Does Acme require a formal procurement milestone (PO) before we run the live traffic phase?
2) Who on your side will sign the evidence items (security/compliance) — procurement or security?
3) Any additional SLA thresholds beyond latency (e.g., token-level cost cap)?

Attaching: MAP_ACME_v1.xlsx, acceptance_test_vignettes.pdf, evidence-index.csv

Thanks — Jordan

--
Jordan Blake

Subject: Re: Mutual action plan: evaluation tests, exit owners & go/no-go timeline

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear write-up. Quick answers inline:
- Procurement: we need an initial SOW/PO to schedule vendor onboarding with our cloud team. I can escalate to procurement to get a draft PO by 7/02.
- Evidence sign-off: security (Ravi) will sign SOC2 and network diagrams. Product will sign acceptance results (myself). Procurement signs commercial docs.
- Cost cap: product team wants an estimated max token spend for the evaluation; can Redwood provide a projected spend range if we hit expected QPS?

Regarding the acceptance tests in your spreadsheet: good start. A couple asks from our side: 
- Can you add a small set of adversarial prompts (5) to the vignettes to test hallucination modes?
- We need a clear rollback trigger if latency >500ms P95 for >4 consecutive hours during the pilot.

I can join the alignment call next Tuesday. Ravi will send a short security questionnaire this afternoon — please loop Priyom on responses.

Thanks — Claire

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mutual action plan: evaluation tests, exit owners & go/no-go timeline

Claire —

Adding technical granularity to what's in the spreadsheet so we have an actionable acceptance test set that product, security and procurement can all sign off on. Below are the acceptance tests and the proposed owner/evidence for each exit gate. I also included fail-fast thresholds and monitoring hooks.

1) Core intent functional correctness (owner: Acme product / evidence: test-pass CSV + sample transcripts)
   - Acceptance test: end-to-end intent match >= 95% over 1,000 labelled prompts (stratified by intent).
   - Data: acceptance_test_vignettes.pdf contains 200 canonical prompts; we will coordinate to label an additional 800 from your telemetry sample.

2) Accuracy / hallucination tolerance (owner: Acme product + Redwood SRE / evidence: hallucination audit report)
   - Acceptance test: hallucination incidents <= 2% on labelled evaluation set (adversarial set included).
   - Adversarial vectors: 5 targeted vignettes provided; Redwood will add 10 synthetic adversarial variants during the run.

3) Latency SLOs (owner: Redwood infra team / evidence: per-route P95/P99 traces in Console)
   - Acceptance test: P95 response latency < 350ms in your staging simulated traffic; P95 < 500ms in pilot with live traffic.
   - Fail-fast: if P95 > 500ms for 4 continuous hours (as Claire requested) we trigger rollback to lighter model variant and run postmortem.

4) Reliability & throughput (owner: Redwood SRE + Acme infra)
   - Acceptance test: sustained throughput of 40 qps for 30 minutes with error rate <1%.

5) Security & evidence (owner: Acme security + Redwood SOC)
   - Acceptance test: signed evidence items for SOC2 scope items 2.1, 3.4 (network segmentation, logging) submitted before go/no-go review.

6) Observability & instrumentation (owner: Marissa Cole / evidence: Console links + export CSV)
   - Acceptance test: token-level cost telemetry enabled; shared dashboard with latency, token counts, and model variant breakdown.

Decision cadence and owners (summary):
- Weekly sync: Wednesday 10am PT (Jordan/Claire/Priyom/Marissa) — status, blockers, evidence on-track
- Midpoint checkpoint: 2025-07-28 — informal readout (pass/fail per-category)
- Final go/no-go meeting: 2025-08-18 — decision owner: Claire (product), sign-off by Ravi (security) and Procurement (PO accepted).

I've updated MAP_ACME_v1.xlsx with the owner column and added the fail-fast rows (see tab: Exit_Gates). Loading these acceptance tests into our evaluation harness will take ~3 business days once you confirm the telemetry sample. We can produce a projected cost range if you share expected QPS and average prompt length — Jordan, can you run cost scenarios for their estimated profile?

Priyom

--
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is great. Next steps from Redwood:

- Priyom will publish the updated acceptance test matrix to the shared Drive (Exit_Gates tab) and we will load the 200 canonical vignettes into the harness once Acme confirms the telemetry sample.
- Marissa will provision a shared Console dashboard and create the evidence export (CSV) for weekly checks.

Action items assigned:
- Claire / Acme: confirm telemetry sample and indicate whether procurement needs the SOW/PO draft by 2025-07-02 (Procurement: procure@acmehealth.com)
- Ravi: send the security questionnaire to priYom; we'll return responses within 3 business days
- Jordan: share cost scenarios by 2025-06-20 EOD

If that timeline looks ok on your end, I'll convert this thread into a MAP doc in Drive and schedule the weekly sync.

Cheers — Jordan
